new_statements.quote: 3.3 Tone. Stevenson considered all three languages have a three-tone system, a claim re-asserted in Yip (2004). Stevenson notes the following contrasts for Keiga Jirru; álè I hoe / álé I say / ále to suck. Stevenson transcribed his data without glide tones but these are almost certainly present. Yip (2004) notes for Tese; Falling tone mâl porcupine, âr path; Rising tone ɗǎl child. However, Dimmendaal (p.c.) considers a system of High/Low plus non-automatic Downstep a better description of the system and inconsistencies in Stevenson's tone-marking do suggest this would be a more credible interpretation.

The quoted passage is there verbatim; the only differences are layout (the Keiga Jirru triplet ale 'I hoe / I say / to suck' and the Tese falling/rising examples are set as small tables, line-break hyphenation 'non-/automatic', and the reader added a…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Temein (with Keiga Jirru and Tese) is described as a lexical tone language: three level tones per Stevenson and Yip, or High/Low plus non-automatic downstep per Dimmendaal. The source says nothing at all about word stress or accent placement; no accessible description of Temein proper makes any stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the only qualification is the competing tonal analyses (3 levels vs. H/L + downstep) and that Stevenson's tone marking is inconsistent.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on words in citation form (wordlist data); no phrase-level prosody discussed. The three-tone claim is stated for all three Temein-cluster languages including Temein proper; the illustrative minimal triplet is Keiga Jirru.
new_statements.identity_note: Blench's paper treats the whole Temein cluster (Temein proper = nucl1339, plus Keiga Jirru/Doni and Tese = tese1238); the tone illustration he cites is from Keiga Jirru (Stevenson) and Tese (Yip 2004), while the claim 'all three languages have a three-tone system' explicitly includes Temein proper. Yip 2004 (OPSL 9, already on file) describes Tese/These (tese1238), not Temein proper.
